$comment: Movement/combat parity scenarios: one timed input script, run identically
against the retail client (Wine rig) and holtburger, so oracle-diff.mjs can
put the two curves side by side.
KEY MAP (holtburger, index.html ~:10967): w/s = forward axis, d/a = strafe
axis, e/q = turn axis, shift = WALK modifier. holtburger is run-by-default
and shift eases to walk; retail is the same convention. So 'walk-hold' is
W+Shift and 'run-hold' is W alone. A driver that gets this backwards will
produce a clean-looking report full of gait-swapped garbage, so both drivers
assert the gait they believe they requested against the telemetry's `gait`
field before any metric is computed.
TIMEBASE: every `t` is milliseconds from scenario start (the first input
event, not process start). `settle_ms` is dead time before that zero point,
to let the avatar come to rest so a scenario never inherits the previous
one's velocity.
METRICS: `expect` slots are DELIBERATELY EMPTY of values. This file is the
question, not the answer — retail supplies the numbers, and oracle-diff.mjs
writes them into retail-pins.json. Hardcoding guesses here would let a
wrong-but-plausible number become the pin and silently define parity as
whatever we already do. `unit` and `tolerance` ARE specified, because those
are decisions about what counts as a difference, not claims about behavior.

steady_speed.how: median planar speed over the steady window (after the ramp, before release)

accel_t90.how: time from the first non-zero speed sample to the first sample at >=90% of steady_speed

decel_t10.how: time from key release to the first sample at <=10% of steady_speed

turn_rate.how: median d(heading)/dt over the steady window, unwrapped across the 0/360 seam

jump_apex.how: max z minus z at launch

jump_airtime.how: launch to the first grounded sample after apex

jump_distance.how: planar distance travelled between launch and land

cast_lock_ms.how: from cast start to the first sample where movement input is honoured again

cast_speed_during.how: median planar speed while the cast window is active

scenarios.description: Hold walk (W+Shift) in a straight line. Establishes the walk steady speed and the walk accel ramp.
Hold run (W, no shift) in a straight line. The reference curve for run speed and ramp; also the T3 mission-bar scenario together with jump-running.

The MOVE-F2 case. Install a walk drive, release it, then take a FRESH key edge with no shift held — which must come back as RUN. Before F2, ingest_key_edge seeded the composed drive from active_drive wholesale (gait included), so the earlier walk poisoned the gait and every later edge stayed stuck in walk. Retail re-derives the gait from the interpreter's hold_run, so retail's second hold is a run. This scenario is the regression pin for that.

The MOVE-F6 case. W+D held together: both axes are issued as concurrent motions and summed, so the ground diagonal EXCEEDS the single-axis run speed. a2's DEVIATION D1 established that retail does NOT cap this on the ground path (get_state_velocity's only caller is get_leave_ground_velocity), so the diagonal running hot is CORRECT and this scenario pins how hot.
Hold W and E together: forward locomotion plus a turn command. Pins the turn rate under load and whether forward speed is reduced while turning.

Standing jump from rest, full charge. Pins apex and airtime with no horizontal component. Relevant to a2's Handoff 1: manual_intent_velocity hands back a GROUND vector for the charged launch, so a charged jump may launch hot; the standing case isolates the vertical term from that.

Jump while at steady run. Pins the airborne trajectory lock — retail freezes the launch velocity for the whole arc, so this is where a hot launch velocity shows up as a long jump. Second half of the T3 mission bar.
Cast from rest. Pins the movement-lock window: how long after cast start the avatar refuses movement input.
Cast at steady run without releasing W. Pins whether the cast arrests movement, and for how long — the case where a lock that is too long or too short is most visible.
Toggle combat stance while holding run. Stance changes the motion style dword and can change the run animation and speed; this pins whether speed survives the switch.
